highlights.title: Don't give bolus when a remote meal is rejected
changes: Rejected remote meal entries no longer cause the meal's explicit bolus to be delivered.
If a remote meal includes a requested bolus, insulin is only delivered after the meal is validated and stored.
Standalone direct bolus commands are unaffected and behave the same.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1347: Do not enact a meal's explicit bolus when the meal is rejected

items.title: Enable algorithm (oref) use from command line
changes: This change does not alter any user-facing features or app behavior.
Developers can now run the oref algorithm and its tests from the command line.
Project and package files were updated and some model adapters were moved so the algorithm builds standalone.
A small logging shim and Decimal helper functions were added to support the standalone algorithm package.

includedPullRequests.title: Do not enact a meal's explicit bolus when the meal is rejected
includedPullRequests.body:
## Summary

For a remote meal command with `bolusAmount`, the `.meal` dispatch calls `handleMealCommand` and then enacts the bolus whenever `bolusAmount != nil`. Since `handleMealCommand` reports validation failures by logging and returning (it doesn't throw), a rejected meal still delivers its bolus. Carbs over the configured max is the easiest way to hit it.

This moves the bolus decision inside `handleMealCommand`, after the meal has validated and stored, so an early return also suppresses the bolus. The standalone `bolus` command is unchanged.

## Background

The max-carbs check exists to catch fat-fingered remote entries, but today it rejects the carbs and delivers the insulin anyway. The caregiver sees a rejection notification and has no reason to think a bolus went through. Found while reviewing the remote meal path for our daughter's caregiver setup.

I'm @justmaier on the Trio Discord if it's easier to discuss there.

Fixes #1349

includedPullRequests.title: Refactor to enable oref from CLI tools
includedPullRequests.body:
This change does a small refactor to enable us to run oref functions
from the CLI. By running oref functions from a CLI we can do more
extensive testing on the algorithm by replaying recorded inputs.

Any CLI programs we write will need to import the Trio package as
@testable for now. If we want to change that later, we'll need to add
`public` annotations to key functions and data structures to be able
to access them.
